On 29 September 2026 Kestrel Semiconductor announced a five-year agreement with TSMC for N3P wafer capacity, 24,000 wafers a month from Q3 2027, plus advanced-packaging slots. Kestrel will pay a US$1.1 billion prepayment and gave no margin guidance. Under the previous contract, Kestrel paid about US$19,800 for each N3P wafer. claims.text: Kestrel Semiconductor lost a fifth of its consensus gross margin in a single morning. On 1 October 2026, the average fiscal 2027 gross margin estimate across the five brokers covering the Singapore-based fabless designer fell to 55.2% from 58.5%, after three of the five revised their models to absorb the terms of a new wafer supply agreement with TSMC. The stock closed 4.1% lower in Taipei, its worst session since February.

The revisions were not a judgment on demand. They were arithmetic. Under the previous contract, Kestrel paid about US$19,800 for each N3P wafer. The new agreement, signed on 29 September and disclosed in a brief filing before the Taipei open, prices the same wafer at roughly US$22,500. That is a rise of 13.6%, and it lands directly on a product line that accounts for the majority of Kestrel's data-center accelerator volume.

Kestrel agreed to advance US$1.1 billion against future wafer deliveries, payable in three instalments, the last of them due by the end of April 2027. Against Kestrel's US$2.4 billion of cash and short-term investments, that is about 46% of the balance sheet committed to a single supplier. Daniel Okafor, who covers the name for Kestrel's most cautious broker, described the structure as "a capacity option dressed as a purchase order" and cut his target price to NT$410 from NT$520.

The timing of the disclosure has a macro dimension that Kestrel's investors did not ask for. The yen's slide past 165 against the dollar has made TSMC's Japanese advanced packaging subsidiary, AP1, more cost-competitive in dollar terms, and the Bank of Japan's reluctance to tighten further has kept the currency weak. TSMC has used that cost advantage to hold the line on packaging prices even as wafer prices rise. For Kestrel, that is a small mercy: the packaging step on the K2 is quoted in yen, and the currency move offsets perhaps 80 basis points of the wafer increase.

Kestrel ended the September quarter with US$2.4 billion in cash and short-term investments and no debt. The US$1.1 billion prepayment is affordable. It is not free. The company had earmarked roughly US$700 million of that cash for a share repurchase program announced in July, and the buyback is now expected to be halved or suspended. Okafor estimates the forgone repurchase adds about 1.5% to fiscal 2028 earnings per share dilution, a figure he called "annoying but not thesis-changing."

The more consequential question is what happens if the K2 slips. The prepayment is not refundable, and the take-or-pay volumes begin in the December 2027 quarter. If Kestrel's own customers push out their orders, the company eats the wafers or pays for them anyway. That scenario is not in any published model, but it is the reason the stock's implied volatility on twelve-month options jumped to 48% from 36% on the day of the filing.

Analysts had expected a price increase. TSMC has been vocal about N3 and N3P capacity being effectively sold out through 2027, and Kestrel is not large enough to command the discounts available to the hyperscaler in-house design teams. What the market did not expect was the prepayment.

claims.text: On 29 September 2026 Kestrel Semiconductor announced a five-year agreement with TSMC for N3P wafer capacity, 24,000 wafers a month from Q3 2027, plus advanced-packaging slots. The disclosure was made in an exchange filing published before the opening of trading. Kestrel will pay a US$1.1 billion prepayment and gave no margin guidance. The previous contract covered 16,000 wafers a month.

According to the filing, the N3P wafers will be produced at TSMC's Fab 18 in Tainan. The first commercial deliveries are expected in the third quarter of 2027. Kestrel said the ramp will be phased, with the full 24,000 wafers a month reached by the second quarter of 2028. The advanced-packaging slots cover CoWoS and InFO processes, also at TSMC facilities in Taiwan.

Kestrel will pay a US$1.1 billion prepayment to TSMC. The filing states that the prepayment is non-refundable and will be credited against future wafer purchases over the five-year term. The first installment of US$400 million is due by 29 October 2026. The second and third installments of US$350 million each are due by 31 January 2027 and 30 April 2027, respectively.

The company said the prepayment will be funded from existing cash and a new revolving credit facility. Kestrel reported cash and equivalents of US$2.3 billion as of 30 June 2026. The filing does not disclose the interest rate or covenants of the credit facility.

Kestrel's previous exchange filing on 15 March 2026 disclosed a letter of intent with TSMC for N3P capacity. That filing did not specify volumes or prepayment amounts. The 29 September 2026 filing supersedes the letter of intent.

On 2 August 2026, Kestrel filed its second-quarter results, reporting revenue of NT$18.4 billion and a gross margin of 34.2 percent. The company did not update those figures in the latest filing. Kestrel's next scheduled disclosure is its third-quarter results on 12 November 2026.

The filing states that the agreement runs for five years from the start of volume production. Kestrel said the prepayment is scheduled in three installments, with the first due within thirty days of signing. The company did not disclose the per-wafer price or the total contract value beyond the prepayment figure.

The filing is available on the Taiwan Stock Exchange's Market Observation Post System under reference number 2026-09-29-001. Kestrel Semiconductor is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange under ticker 6415. TSMC is listed under ticker 2330.

sources.title: Kestrel Semiconductor exchange filing: TSMC capacity agreement
sources.body:
## Filing summary

On 29 September 2026 Kestrel Semiconductor announced a five-year agreement with TSMC for N3P wafer capacity, 24,000 wafers a month from Q3 2027, plus advanced-packaging slots. The disclosure was made in an exchange filing published before the opening of trading. Kestrel will pay a US$1.1 billion prepayment and gave no margin guidance. The previous contract covered 16,000 wafers a month.

The filing states that the agreement runs for five years from the start of volume production. Kestrel said the prepayment is scheduled in three installments, with the first due within thirty days of signing. The company did not disclose the per-wafer price or the total contract value beyond the prepayment figure.

## Capacity and timing

According to the filing, the N3P wafers will be produced at TSMC's Fab 18 in Tainan. The first commercial deliveries are expected in the third quarter of 2027. Kestrel said the ramp will be phased, with the full 24,000 wafers a month reached by the second quarter of 2028. The advanced-packaging slots cover CoWoS and InFO processes, also at TSMC facilities in Taiwan.

The previous contract, signed in 2023, covered 16,000 wafers a month on the N5 process. Kestrel said the new agreement replaces that contract upon its expiration in June 2027. The filing notes that the N3P process offers higher transistor density and lower power consumption than N5, but does not provide performance figures.

## Prepayment terms

Kestrel will pay a US$1.1 billion prepayment to TSMC. The filing states that the prepayment is non-refundable and will be credited against future wafer purchases over the five-year term. The first installment of US$400 million is due by 29 October 2026. The second and third installments of US$350 million each are due by 31 January 2027 and 30 April 2027, respectively.

The company said the prepayment will be funded from existing cash and a new revolving credit facility. Kestrel reported cash and equivalents of US$2.3 billion as of 30 June 2026. The filing does not disclose the interest rate or covenants of the credit facility.

## Financial guidance

Kestrel gave no margin guidance in the filing. The company said it will provide updated financial targets at its next earnings call, scheduled for 12 November 2026. The filing does not include revenue or earnings forecasts related to the agreement.

The filing gives no guidance on how the agreement affects gross margin or wafer pricing, and Kestrel did not comment on analyst coverage.

## Market and regulatory context

The filing was made under the exchange's rules for material contracts. Kestrel's shares closed at NT$487.50 on 28 September 2026, the day before the announcement. The Taiwan Stock Exchange requires listed companies to disclose contracts that may affect shareholder equity by more than 5 percent.

TSMC declined to comment beyond confirming the agreement. The Bank of Japan's quarterly Tankan survey, released on 1 October 2026, will include capital expenditure plans for the semiconductor sector. Kestrel said it has not received any regulatory objections to the agreement.

The filing states that the agreement includes a force majeure clause and a dispute resolution mechanism under Singapore law. Kestrel said it does not expect the agreement to have a material impact on its operations in the current fiscal year.

## Prior disclosures

Kestrel's previous exchange filing on 15 March 2026 disclosed a letter of intent with TSMC for N3P capacity. That filing did not specify volumes or prepayment amounts. The 29 September 2026 filing supersedes the letter of intent.

On 2 August 2026, Kestrel filed its second-quarter results, reporting revenue of NT$18.4 billion and a gross margin of 34.2 percent. The company did not update those figures in the latest filing. Kestrel's next scheduled disclosure is its third-quarter results on 12 November 2026.

The filing is available on the Taiwan Stock Exchange's Market Observation Post System under reference number 2026-09-29-001. Kestrel Semiconductor is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange under ticker 6415. TSMC is listed under ticker 2330.

sources.title: Analysts cut Kestrel margin estimates as the TSMC deal lands
sources.body:
Kestrel Semiconductor lost a fifth of its consensus gross margin in a single morning. On 1 October 2026, the average fiscal 2027 gross margin estimate across the five brokers covering the Singapore-based fabless designer fell to 55.2% from 58.5%, after three of the five revised their models to absorb the terms of a new wafer supply agreement with TSMC. The stock closed 4.1% lower in Taipei, its worst session since February.

The revisions were not a judgment on demand. They were arithmetic. Under the previous contract, Kestrel paid about US$19,800 for each N3P wafer. The new agreement, signed on 29 September and disclosed in a brief filing before the Taipei open, prices the same wafer at roughly US$22,500. That is a rise of 13.6%, and it lands directly on a product line that accounts for the majority of Kestrel's data-center accelerator volume.

## The prepayment is the part that worries the buy side

Analysts had expected a price increase. TSMC has been vocal about N3 and N3P capacity being effectively sold out through 2027, and Kestrel is not large enough to command the discounts available to the hyperscaler in-house design teams. What the market did not expect was the prepayment.

Kestrel agreed to advance US$1.1 billion against future wafer deliveries, payable in three instalments, the last of them due by the end of April 2027. Against Kestrel's US$2.4 billion of cash and short-term investments, that is about 46% of the balance sheet committed to a single supplier. Daniel Okafor, who covers the name for Kestrel's most cautious broker, described the structure as "a capacity option dressed as a purchase order" and cut his target price to NT$410 from NT$520.

The bull case is that the prepayment locks in allocation at a moment when N3P slots are the scarcest input in the accelerator supply chain. Kestrel's next-generation part, the K2, is scheduled to tape out in the June 2027 quarter and ramps in volume in fiscal 2028. Without secured capacity, the company would be bidding for scraps on the spot market, where lead times have stretched past forty weeks. With it, Kestrel can promise customers delivery dates, which in this market is worth more than a few points of gross margin.

## Revenue estimates went up, not down

The same morning produced a second, less-noticed revision. Analysts raised fiscal 2028 revenue estimates to US$6.4 billion from US$5.5 billion on 1 October 2026, citing the volume commitments embedded in the TSMC agreement. The contract's take-or-pay structure implies wafer purchases consistent with roughly 40% more accelerator shipments than the previous model assumed.

That combination, higher revenue and lower margin, is the classic signature of a company trading profitability for scale. Mei-Ling Tan of the Taipei desk at a regional brokerage raised her fiscal 2028 revenue number by 16% while cutting her gross margin assumption by 310 basis points. "The mix is shifting toward a larger, lower-margin customer set," she wrote. "We would rather own the volume than the margin, but we are not going to pretend the margin is intact."

Two of the five analysts kept their margin estimates unchanged, arguing that the price increase will be offset by a richer product mix in the second half of fiscal 2027, when the higher-margin K2 variant enters production. Both, however, flagged the prepayment as a risk factor in their notes. The consensus, for now, sits with the majority.

## What the Bank of Japan has to do with it

The timing of the disclosure has a macro dimension that Kestrel's investors did not ask for. The yen's slide past 165 against the dollar has made TSMC's Japanese advanced packaging subsidiary, AP1, more cost-competitive in dollar terms, and the Bank of Japan's reluctance to tighten further has kept the currency weak. TSMC has used that cost advantage to hold the line on packaging prices even as wafer prices rise. For Kestrel, that is a small mercy: the packaging step on the K2 is quoted in yen, and the currency move offsets perhaps 80 basis points of the wafer increase.

But the BoJ is the wild card. If the central bank signals a faster normalization path at its December meeting, the yen strengthens, AP1's dollar costs rise, and TSMC has historically passed such moves through to fabless customers at the next contract reset. Kestrel's agreement runs through fiscal 2029, but it contains a currency-adjustment clause that two of the analysts flagged as under-modeled.

## The cash question

Kestrel ended the September quarter with US$2.4 billion in cash and short-term investments and no debt. The US$1.1 billion prepayment is affordable. It is not free. The company had earmarked roughly US$700 million of that cash for a share repurchase program announced in July, and the buyback is now expected to be halved or suspended. Okafor estimates the forgone repurchase adds about 1.5% to fiscal 2028 earnings per share dilution, a figure he called "annoying but not thesis-changing."

The more consequential question is what happens if the K2 slips. The prepayment is not refundable, and the take-or-pay volumes begin in the December 2027 quarter. If Kestrel's own customers push out their orders, the company eats the wafers or pays for them anyway. That scenario is not in any published model, but it is the reason the stock's implied volatility on twelve-month options jumped to 48% from 36% on the day of the filing.

For now, the sell side has done what the sell side does: marked the margin down, marked the revenue up, and moved on. The next data point is Kestrel's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on 12 November, when management is expected to give its first formal guidance for fiscal 2027. Until then, the 55.2% consensus is a placeholder, and everyone knows it.
